- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.11) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 5–7 days.  
- If recent price history shows sharp upward moves followed by rapid decline (e.g., spike then drop), model often overshoots downward; adjust downward by 1–3% in next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.28) and price is trending down, model often underestimates the drop; increase forecast downward by 1–2% for next 5–7 days.  
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment spikes; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day moving average) to forecast if sentiment volatility > 0.20.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 65–70), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day moving average of true values.  
- For horizon > 14 days, model often underestimates downward trends; apply 1–2% downward bias if sentiment is neutral or negative.  
- If sentiment is flat (0.00–0.06) and price is trending sideways, model often overestimates volatility; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 7–10 days.
